questions.q: Why can a purely timestamp-based incremental sync leave deleted Salesforce records in the warehouse?
options: Timestamps cannot be read through any API
Salesforce never allows deletion
A deleted record doesn't appear as a changed row, so the sync never learns about it
Incremental syncs always reload everything
questions.explain: Deletes need separate handling, such as syncing the deleted flag, periodic full refreshes, or comparing Ids.

questions.q: What is the main problem if a downstream job runs before its upstream sync finishes?
options: It processes stale data and often shows no visible error
Salesforce blocks the account
The dashboard becomes read-only
It doubles the API limit
questions.explain: Dependency-aware scheduling and failure alerts prevent silent staleness.

questions.q: What should freshness targets be based on?
options: Always real time, for every dataset
What each decision or dashboard actually needs, agreed with the business
Whatever the default schedule happens to be
The number of fields in the object
questions.explain: Tighter freshness costs more, so match the target to the business need and write it down.

questions.q: A data stream's refresh history shows several successful runs that processed zero records over many days. What does this suggest?
options: Everything is perfectly healthy
The dashboard is faster than usual
The stream can never be deleted
It is worth investigating, because success status doesn't prove new data is flowing
questions.explain: Zero-record runs can be normal if nothing changed, but a persistent pattern deserves a check against the source.

questions.q: Which is a sound reconciliation practice?
options: Only compare screenshots of dashboards
Assume the warehouse is right because it is bigger
Compare row counts and key sums between the warehouse and an equivalent Salesforce aggregate on a schedule
Reconcile once at project launch and never again
questions.explain: Regular counts and sums, plus checking the latest SystemModstamp, catch drift early; persistent gaps indicate a problem.
